extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent prosecution practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs), Office actions, citation of prior art, and related examiner responsibilities under USPTO rules (MPEP). Covers eligibility, timing, form paragraphs, search and citation practices, and supervisory responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Continued Examination under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice is not applicable to provisional applications, design applications, applications filed before June 8, 1995, or during reexamination. See MPEP references cited for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a Proper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) and the submission required by 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee and/or submission are missing the RCE is improper. Where a submission accompanies an RCE but the fee is missing, include a statement whether the submission has been entered; generally such submissions should not be entered, except amendments that obviously place the application in condition for allowance (with supervisory approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of RCE filings relative to appeals and civil actions
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE may be filed after a decision by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences but before filing a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or the commencement of a civil action; RCE practice is not available after the filing of a Notice of Appeal or commencement of a civil action unless the appeal/civil action is terminated and the application is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed in an application that has undergone court review, the examiner should bring the application to the attention of the supervisory patent examiner or special program examiner to determine propriety. Termination of an unsuccessful appeal or civil action generally results in abandonment unless claims were allowed or the court's mandate directs further Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Improper RCEs (use of form paragraph 7.42.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE filed after a Board decision lacks the required fee and/or submission, the RCE is improper and any time period running was not tolled by filing the improper request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.16 to notify the applicant. If time for seeking court review has passed, include the paragraph with the mailing of a Notice of Allowability or Abandonment as appropriate; if time remains include the paragraph on a PTOL-90 and set no time period. State whether any submission filed with an improper RCE has been entered (e.g., 'The submission filed with the improper RCE has not been entered.').

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Board Decision (res judicata / law of the case)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences decision in an application has res judicata effect and is the 'law of the case' and thus is controlling in that application and any subsequent, related application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A submission containing only arguments (without an amendment of the rejected claims or a showing of facts) will not be effective to remove such rejection; see MPEP §§ 706.03(w) and 1214.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctions among CPA, URAA 1.129(a), and RCE 1.114 procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The RCE procedure (37 CFR 1.114), CPA procedure (37 CFR 1.53(d)), and URAA transitional procedure (37 CFR 1.129(a)) are distinct processes with different applicability, timing, fees, and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare each on: applicability to application types and filing dates; whether practice constitutes continued examination of same application or is a new application (CPA is technically new, RCE/1.129(a) are continued examination of same application); whether filing fee deferral is allowed; entitlement to patent term adjustment; limits on number of filings/submissions; certificate of mailing entitlement; and other differences shown in the MPEP comparison chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing timing requirements (CPA vs URAA vs RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA may be filed before prosecution is closed; a URAA 1.129(a) submission must be filed after final rejection and before an appeal brief is filed; an RCE must be filed after prosecution in an application is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These timing differences affect whether appeals become moot, abandonment consequences, and entitlement to various statutory benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee rules and patent term adjustment effects for CPA/URAA/RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office sets the RCE fee at an amount equal to the basic filing fee of a utility application (small entity reduction available); RCE fee need not include excess claims fees previously paid. Filing an RCE on or after May 29, 2000 will not cause an application to be entitled to patent term adjustment provisions of the AIPA; filing an RCE cuts off the applicant's ability to accumulate additional patent term adjustment against the three‑year pendency provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA and URAA fee rules and patent term adjustment entitlements differ: CPA fees must be statutory filing fee (basic filing fee plus excess claim fees) and CPA filed on/after May 29, 2000 is entitled to patent term adjustment provisions under the AIPA in specified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on number of filings/submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the number of times an applicant may file a CPA or an RCE to obtain continued examination; under 37 CFR 1.129(a) an applicant may have only two submissions entered as a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different procedures impose different quantitative limits—consult the specific rule for the procedure being used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on inventorship and small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventorship carries over/continues across CPA, URAA, and RCE practice (any change must be via 37 CFR 1.48). Small entity status rules vary: small entity status does not carry for CPA (must be claimed or paid), but small entity status may carry/continue in some situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the MPEP table and applicable statutes/regulations for exact treatment in each procedural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission content requirement: bona fide attempt to advance the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain continued examination/transitional submissions must include a reply that is a bona fide attempt to advance the application, as required by 37 CFR 1.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a submission must include such a reply depends on the procedure and whether a reply to an Office action is outstanding; refer to specific rule citations in the MPEP table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty: thorough study and prior art investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application for examination the examiner shall make a thorough study thereof and shall make a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention; the examination shall be complete with respect to compliance with applicable statutes and rules and to the patentability of the invention as claimed, as well as matters of form unless otherwise indicated (37 CFR 1.104).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The search should identify the best references on the first search and be complete; assistance may include international-type search on request and fee where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action and scope limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder of invention, fundamental defects) the action may be limited to such matters before further action is made. Matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations on scope should be applied only in appropriate circumstances; supervisory review is expected in protracted prosecutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting claims: cite best references and explain pertinence
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, the claims considered unpatentable will be rejected. In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command and, when a reference is complex or shows inventions other than that claimed, designate the particular part relied on as nearly as practicable. The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified (37 CFR 1.104(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rejecting under 35 U.S.C. 103, the way in which a reference is modified or plural references are combined should be set out. Include particular figures/pages/paragraphs when necessary to inform applicant of the basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and Office employee knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant (or patent owner in reexamination) as to any matter affecting patentability and may rely upon facts within his or her knowledge under certain regulatory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an Office employee, the data shall be as specific as possible and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee; such affidavit is subject to contradiction or explanation by applicant affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f),(g) in 103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person that qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned by the same person or organization or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person or organization at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully analyze ownership/assignment status before relying on such prior art in §103 rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of references: required bibliographic and locating details
rubrics_metrics.description: When domestic patents are cited, their numbers and dates and names of patentees must be stated. For domestic patent application publications, state publication number, publication date, and names of applicants. For foreign published applications/patents, give nationality/country, numbers and dates, names of patentees, and other data necessary for identification; where only part of a foreign document is involved, identify particular pages and sheets. For printed publications give author, title, date, pages or plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient bibliographic detail to enable applicant to identify and obtain the cited material.

rubrics_metrics.name: When rejection is based on Office personal knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an Office employee, the supporting data shall be as specific as possible and, when requested, supported by the employee's affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such affidavits are subject to contradiction or explanation by applicant and others; ensure specificity and documentary support where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance: documenting examiner rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes the record of the prosecution does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim, the examiner may set forth such reasoning; the reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or be the subject of a separate communication. The applicant may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure by the examiner to respond to any statement commenting on reasons for allowance does not give rise to any implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office actions must provide adequate detail and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions should state reasons for any adverse action, objections, or requirements and give information or references useful to aid applicant to judge propriety of continuing prosecution. Where necessary, include particular figures/pages/paragraphs of references and brief relevant comments. For 103 rejections, explain how references are modified or combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exceptional cases and pro se cases a more complete explanation may be needed. Attach Notice of References Cited (PTO-892) and other attachments; use Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 for first actions and conclude actions with one of form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101, or 7.102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite and explain relevant prior art and consider IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should cite appropriate prior art which is nearest to the subject matter defined in the claims, and when such prior art is cited its relevance should be explained. The examiner must consider all prior art references (alone and in combination) cited in the application or reexamination, including those cited by the applicant in an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.96 may be used as an introductory sentence; explain relevance in bracketed text per MPEP § 707.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited references: furnishing and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of cited references (except as noted) are automatically furnished without charge to applicant together with the Office action in which they are cited and are placed in the application file for examiner use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where copies are not furnished include documents referred to in applicant's disclosure statement; copies provided in a parent application; documents cited by a third party under 37 CFR 1.99; and U.S. patents cited at allowance. Copies of foreign patent documents and nonpatent literature cited by the examiner at allowance will be furnished to applicant with the Office action and retained in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search practice regarding filing dates and patent term consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should search all applications based on the actual U.S. filing date of the application rather than on the filing date of any parent U.S. application for which benefit is claimed, because the 20-year patent term is measured from the earliest U.S. filing date for which benefit is claimed (Public Law 103-465 changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite material prior art having an effective filing date after the filing date of the U.S. parent application but before the actual filing date of the application being examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed applications should generally cite pertinent prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed applications should generally contain a citation of pertinent prior art for printing in the patent; only where a proper search has not revealed any prior art relevant to the claimed invention is it appropriate to send an application to issue with no art cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no prior art is cited, the examiner must write 'None' on form PTO-892 and insert it in the file wrapper. For continuations, parent application citations should be reviewed and listed when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory examiner responsibilities for long-pendency applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisory patent examiners should personally check the pendency of every application which is up for the third or subsequent official action with a view to finally concluding its prosecution. Any application pending five years should be carefully studied by the supervisory examiner and every effort made to terminate its prosecution; such applications should be considered 'special' by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize finding the best references on the first search and taking steps to conclude prosecution where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner duties when assistant examiner is new
rubrics_metrics.description: When an assistant examiner has been in the Office a short time, the primary examiner must review the application thoroughly, hear the assistant's explanation of the invention and the references considered most pertinent, and indicate the action to be taken (restriction/election, consideration on the merits, how references are to be applied, or allowance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiners should guide new assistants to find the best references and how to apply them; extensive amendments are preferably filed by the applicant's attorney/agent to provide a better file record.
